extracted.intended_audience: literate London readers interested in manners, morals, and literary style (Spectator readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative points for composing short moral/literary essays and stories, and for social conduct as treated in Spectator-style periodical writing. Includes criteria for narrative effect (surprise, delivery) and for moral/social behaviour (politeness, respect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit the length of hope
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a Precept ... that we should not entertain an Hope of any thing in Life which lies at a great Distance from us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because life is short and uncertain ("The Grave lies unseen between us and the Object"), hoping for distant objects is unreasonable and often leads to disappointment. Prefer goods within reasonable reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh the value of the object of hope
rubrics_metrics.description: We should sufficiently weigh the Objects of our Hope, whether they be such as we may reasonably expect from them what we propose in their Fruition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the object will actually deliver the satisfaction you expect; failing to assess its true value increases disappointment when attained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess attainability given life's uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: We should ... consider whether they are such as we are pretty sure of attaining, in case our Life extend itself so far.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate the likelihood you will live to enjoy the hoped-for good; avoid plans that depend on improbably long life or unlikely contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid endless extension of hopes
rubrics_metrics.description: One Hope no sooner dies in us but another rises up in its stead ... we have no sooner gained one Point but we extend our Hopes to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise the tendency to move the goalposts: gaining one object often seeds a new, more distant desire. This continual extension makes life a "greater Dream and Shadow" and breeds discontent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise is the life of stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Surprize is so much the Life of Stories, that every one aims at it, who endeavours to please by telling them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To please an audience, aim to include an element of surprise—unexpected turns that arrest attention and give stories vitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use smooth delivery, elegant diction, and arrangement as beautifying graces
rubrics_metrics.description: Smooth Delivery, an elegant Choice of Words, and a sweet Arrangement, are all beautifying Graces, but not the particulars ... which either long command the Attention, or strike with the Violence of a sudden Passion, or occasion the burst of Laughter which accompanies Humour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polish (delivery, word choice, arrangement) improves a tale, but these are secondary to the concrete particulars that generate sustained interest, strong emotion, or humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include particulars that command attention (sustained interest, passion, humour)
rubrics_metrics.description: The particulars ... either long command the Attention, or strike with the Violence of a sudden Passion, or occasion the burst of Laughter which accompanies Humour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop vivid particulars or incidents that either hold attention over time, produce sudden emotional impact, or provoke laughter—these are the effective engines of narrative engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politeness and restraint in public/company conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints about persons in Stage-Coaches who attack'd me with such indecent Discourse ... form to your self what a Persecution this must needs be to a virtuous and a chaste Mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers should refrain from indecent or lewd discourse in mixed company; social etiquette requires protecting the modest and vulnerable from verbal harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat women as companions, not mere ornaments
rubrics_metrics.description: There is, Sir, a Language particular for talking to Women in; and none but those of the very first good Breeding ... can speak to us without regard to our Sex. ... I love to ask Questions when I fall into such Conversation; but I am cut short ... by something about my bright Eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not flatter or patronise women because of their looks; allow them to speak and be treated as thoughtful companions deserving honest, plain answers rather than constant decorative praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use social rebuke or public sanction to check indecency
rubrics_metrics.description: I humbly propose you would invent some Padlock ... for all modest Persons ... to clap upon the Mouths of all such impertinent impudent Fellows: And I wish you would publish a Proclamation ... that part of the Directions may be, when any Person presumes to be guilty of the above-mentioned Crime, the Party aggrieved may produce it to his Face, with a Request to read it to the Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes public shaming or formalized rebuke (satirical padlock/proclamation) as a remedy: make indecent conduct liable to immediate exposure and social punishment so the offender cannot 'outface' the reproach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage useful occupations for idle fashionable men
rubrics_metrics.description: Since Knotting is again in fashion ... you would recommend it to these Gentlemen as something that may make them useful to the Ladies they admire ... it may be done ... in all Places where they come for the sake of the Ladies ... it shews a white Hand and Diamond Ring to great advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel the idle energies of 'beaus' into harmless, graceful amusements (like knotting) that render them socially useful and less vapid, while fitting with their social habits.
